title: Ashenvale
body: Ashenvale is the great forest of the night elves, ancient trees reaching from Darkshore and Felwood down to the Barrens and Stonetalon. After the Sundering the kaldorei rebuilt their lives beneath its boughs, and for ages the Sentinels patrolled it while the druids slept. The Third War broke that peace: Grom Hellscream's Warsong orcs came to cut its timber and slew the demigod Cenarius. Now the Horde logs the east from Splintertree Post, the Alliance holds Astranaar, and around them furbolgs turn savage, satyrs haunt the ruins and demons linger.

parts.body: In this age draenei of the Hand of Argus help the night elves restore Forest Song, and blood elves have joined the Horde's warriors at Splintertree.

title: Astranaar
body: Astranaar is the chief night elf town of Ashenvale, built on an island in a lake and joined to the shore by bridges on the main road. Raene Wolfrunner, a Sentinel officer never far from her wolf Dagri, directs the struggle against the furbolgs, whose attacks grow bolder, while others send fighters against the naga of the coast. With the Horde building up to the south, the town feels exposed.

parts.body: Raene's friend Teronis died seeking the rod of Dartol, a human wizard who learned druidic magic to walk among the furbolgs in their shape, until they caught him turning tribe against tribe, killed him and split the rod in three.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Astranaar (island in a lake, bridges, largest settlement)

parts.body: The skull of Ran Bloodtooth, the fiercest furbolg threat in Ashenvale, now rests here beside Dartol's rod for all to see. Teronis, Raene says, would be proud.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Astranaar (island in a lake, bridges, largest settlement)

parts.body: Vindicator Palanaar, a draenei paladin, waits here for those of her people sent to aid the night elves, and points them to where help is needed.

title: Maestra's Post
body: Maestra's Post is a small night elf camp on the road through western Ashenvale, and an unusual meeting place, for two humans live here. The paladin Delgren the Purifier lends his strength wherever the Sentinels find demons or undead; the ways of the kaldorei were strange to him at first, but he has come to respect them greatly. North of the post, warlocks of a cult dig among the Ruins of Ordil'Aran.

parts.body: Delgren studies his enemies as closely as he fights them. Against the scoffing of his order he learned the orcish tongue, and with it read the cult's secrets in an orc warlock's writings.

title: The Zoram Strand
body: The Zoram Strand is the long northwestern shore of Ashenvale. Beneath its waves lies Zoram, a night elf city destroyed in the Sundering and swallowed by the sea, and the naga have returned to it for reasons no one knows. At the strand's northern end lies the entrance to Blackfathom Deeps, once a temple of Elune, and to the south the Horde holds Zoram'gar Outpost, the front line, its commander says, of the Horde's conquest of the forest.

parts.body: At Zoram'gar the troll Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring reads the waves and watches the depths of Blackfathom, where the naga harvest crystals of great elemental power.

parts.body: Zoram's rulers once wore a ring said to open any lock in their city. The naga leader Ruuzel found it first, on an isle at the drowned city's northern edge.

title: Splintertree Post
body: Splintertree Post is the Horde's chief outpost in Ashenvale, raised by Grom Hellscream's Warsong clan when the orcs first came into the forest in the Third War. Orcs and tauren hold it, north of the road from the Barrens. From here the Horde supplies its lumber camps and sends raiders against Silverwing Outpost, and Senani Thunderheart calls young hunters to the Ashenvale Hunt, a trial against three legendary beasts of the forest.

parts.body: In this age blood elves are part of the Horde, and their advisor Sunsworn keeps a place at the post, urging her people to help wherever they can to cement their bond with the rest of the Horde.

title: Warsong Lumber Camp
body: In eastern Ashenvale the Warsong fell the ancient trees on a scale the night elves can hardly bear to watch, with peons, deforesters and shredders bought in Ratchet, and a second labor camp works near Fallen Sky Lake. The Horde holds that the night elves would deny it one of its largest sources of lumber. The Silverwing Sentinels call it the ruin of their forest and fight for every grove, while satyrs and furbolgs plunder the camps' supplies.

parts.body: Of late Overseer Gorthak drives his crews harder each time the Sentinels of Forest Song slow them. They now fell more than they can use and leave it to rot, and demons from Felfire Hill raid the camp as well.

title: Forest Song
body: Forest Song is an old night elf shrine in the Nightsong Woods of northeastern Ashenvale, long all but forgotten. The druid Kayneth Stillwind gathers reports of a corruption he fears is moving through the forest, Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow holds the demons of Felwood back from Ashenvale, and the dryad Illiyana waits for sisters who went to win back the Branch of Cenarius from the satyrs.

parts.body: The glade is waking. The kaldorei have invited the draenei to help restore it, and under Architect Nemos tents rise where buildings will one day stand. Nemos will not fell the grove's trees, so the ancient Gnarl purifies timber taken from the Warsong.

title: Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Canyon
body: In Demon Fall Canyon Grom Hellscream and Thrall faced the pit lord Mannoroth, whose blood had first cursed the orcs. Grom struck him down and died in the blast, and the blood curse ended with the demon. A monument raised by Thrall marks where Grom lies, and Mannoroth's broken spear still floats above the canyon. Yet the Legion never wholly left: infernals, felguards and mannoroc roam Felfire Hill, the canyon and the ridge above.

parts.body: At Forest Song the ancient Gnarl has seeds planted in the hill's fertile mounds. It may take many years, but in the fullness of time they will grow into ancients and stand against the demons.

title: The Howling Vale
body: In northern Ashenvale, near the Felwood border, a cave holds the ruined Shrine of Mel'Thandris, where an old inscription still asks Elune to light the ways of the forest forever. Wolf-men fill it now, and their chilling calls gave the vale its name. The shrine keeps the Tome of Mel'Thandris, blessed by Mel'Thandris herself, which shows events of import, though no one truly understands why it shows what it does.

parts.body: The tome shows the priestess Velinde Starsong receiving the Scythe of Elune. Velinde held Felwood's demons back before Melyria, until her efforts faltered and one day she simply disappeared.
sources: quest 1022 description and texts (shrine of Mel'Thandris near the Felwood border overrun by wolf-men, tome blessed by Mel'Thandris, Scythe of Elune)

parts.body: Her journal tells why. Through the scythe she called worgen to fight the demons, but they multiplied beyond her control; she penned the packs here and went to seek Arugal, a wizard said to have called worgen too.
sources: quest 1022 description and texts (shrine of Mel'Thandris near the Felwood border overrun by wolf-men, tome blessed by Mel'Thandris, Scythe of Elune)

parts.body: Velinde was the high priestess's friend, and Thyn'tel Bladeweaver of the Sentinels grieves that the Scythe, surely Elune's own boon, has passed out of her servants' hands.

title: Satyrnaar
body: Satyrnaar was once a prominent shrine of the night elves, whose keepers held the Chalice of Elune and drew pilgrims seeking its healing. Bleakheart satyrs now camp among its ruins under Prince Raze, fouling the very wood with their corruption, and a strange gem glows among their stones. The Felmusk satyrs keep another at Night Run, to the west.

parts.body: The gems are no satyr work: the Cult of the Dark Strand hid its master's last two soul gems in these blood-soaked temples, one in each camp, with Highborne souls trapped inside.
sources: quest 9519 description and reward text (Satyrnaar once a shrine, Chalice of Elune, pilgrims, still shines)

parts.body: Carried out to Kayneth Stillwind at Forest Song, the Chalice of Elune still shines, with a latent power that not even long exposure to the satyrs' corruption could dim.

title: The Dor'Danil Barrow Den
body: South of Splintertree Post lies the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, long a resting place of night elf druids whose spirits walk the Emerald Dream. The Horde's advance left it behind enemy lines, and then the Forsaken came, camping beside it to brew diseases in bottles. Within, the druids no longer sleep: severed sleepers and dreamers haunt the halls, restless and hostile.

parts.body: Kayneth Stillwind tested one of the bottles and, resisting its disease, saw what happened here: the Forsaken poisoned the sleeping druids, tearing their spirits from their bodies and driving them mad.

title: Bough Shadow
body: At the far northeastern edge of Ashenvale, beyond Forest Song, a great tree shelters one of the four portals into the Emerald Dream; the others lie in Duskwood, the Hinterlands and Feralas. Green dragonkin stand guard over it and welcome no visitors.

parts.body: Of late the great green dragon Ysondre herself emerges here at times, crying that the strands of life have been severed and calling on the Dreamers to take their vengeance.
